job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
The Opportunity
Central to the opportunity is the connection between finance and manufacturing performance. You’ll work across operations, sales, and the wider business to turn financial information into practical insight, improve commercial understanding and help maximise performance. You’ll also lead and develop a small finance team while building stronger financial capability beyond the function.

As the Finance Manager you’ll take ownership of the New Zealand finance function within an established international business. Reporting to the local General Manager, this is a hands-on leadership role spanning financial management, reporting, planning, working capital, controls and continuous improvement.

Experience in a manufacturing environment is a critical part of the role. The finance function supports operational decision-making, inventory and working capital management, cost and control disciplines, and ongoing process improvement across the business.

The Company
This organisation is an established international manufacturer with a significant New Zealand operation based in Christchurch. It supplies performance-focused products into the local market and operates within a structured group environment, combining local accountability with divisional and group reporting requirements.

The Role
  • Lead the New Zealand finance function and provide financial direction aligned with business strategy, annual goals and operational priorities
  • Coordinate monthly, quarterly and annual reporting for local leadership and wider group finance, including management accounts, analysis and clear performance commentary
  • Own budgeting, forecasting, strategic planning and longer-term financial modelling, including development of a five-year plan
  • Partner with the General Manager and key stakeholders across manufacturing operations, sales and support functions to improve accountability and financial performance
  • Manage working capital with a strong focus on receivables, inventory holdings and supplier payment terms
  • Maintain robust financial controls, general ledger integrity, audit trails and risk review processes while improving reporting efficiency through systems and technology
  • Lead, coach and develop a small finance team, while improving financial understanding and capability across the wider New Zealand business

Your Profile
  • Chartered Accountant with a bachelor’s degree in accounting or a related discipline
  • Relevant finance experience gained in a commercial environment, with manufacturing experience strongly preferred
  • Strong grounding in management and financial accounting, budgeting, forecasting, reporting and general ledger control
  • Commercial understanding of working capital and the financial drivers of a manufacturing operation, including inventory and operational performance
  • Confident business partner who can communicate clearly with operational teams, customers, suppliers and senior stakeholders
  • Strong Excel and Microsoft Office capability, with practical ERP experience. SAP exposure would be advantageous
  • Sharp attention to detail, a drive to improve accuracy and efficiency, and full, unrestricted working rights for New Zealand

The Opportunity
You’re a commercially minded accountant who likes variety and ownership. You want a role that stretches across month-end, cashflow, tax and fixed assets – and still leaves time to sit with store and support managers and make the numbers useful.
Based in Christchurch and reporting to the the Finance Manager, you’ll own the accounting for a national retail group and a related entity. One day you’re reconciling banks, stores and intercompany balances; the next you’re preparing management accounts, working through GST and FBT, or talking a store or budget holder through their results. If you enjoy being useful to the wider business – not just closing the books – you’ll get a lot from this one.

The Company
This is a confidential search for a well-established, family-owned New Zealand business and a shared-services base in Christchurch. The business is known for quality procucts, with locatons from the top of the North Island to the bottom of the South.

The Role
You’ll work alongside finance business partners, a financial accountant, management accountants and the AP/AR team, with regular contact across stores, logistics, regional managers and the wider support office.
You’ll own the commercial accounting for the group and a related entity, and support the wider finance team. Key responsibilities include:
  • Prepare monthly management accounts and analysis, complete balance sheet reconciliations, and keep daily bank, store and intercompany balances accurate
  • Manage daily cashflow and banking, and assist with cashflow forecasting
  • Lead group fixed asset accounting – monthly depreciation, additions and disposals – and support year-end stocktakes and audit
  • Own New Zealand tax compliance, including GST and FBT
  • Partner with store and budget holders on monthly sales, margin and expense analysis and commentary, and support annual budgets, forecasts and commercial decision-making
  • Act as a key contact for year-end and audit; support inventory provisions, WIP and open purchase order reviews, lease accounting and store-related commercial queries
Your Profile
You’re organised, accurate and commercially curious – someone managers are happy to call. You’ll bring:
  • Completed tertiary study in accounting or finance, plus at least three years’ experience in a commercial finance team of meaningful size
  • Hands-on experience with month-end reporting, bank reconciliations, tax compliance, purchase orders and transactional accounting; multi-site or retail exposure is useful, as is payroll
  • Confident Microsoft Excel (and Word) skills, with experience in an ERP or similar business system an advantage

job.title: Chief Financial Officer
job.description:
The Opportunity
This is a broad finance leadership role within a business that wants finance to play a bigger part in where it goes next.
  
Working alongside the leadership team, you’ll bring greater commercial focus to planning, performance and decision-making across the organisation. Rather than simply reporting on what has already happened, you’ll help the business understand what is driving its results, where the opportunities sit and what may need to change.
  
There is still a hands-on element to the position. You’ll have oversight of the core finance function and will need to be comfortable moving between strategic conversations, commercial analysis and the practical realities of running finance in a busy organisation.
  
It’s a role with genuine breadth and visibility, offering the opportunity to influence business direction while remaining closely connected to operational performance and financial delivery.
  
The Company
You’ll be joining an established New Zealand organisation with a solid foundation and a clear appetite to keep improving.
  
The working environment is practical, collaborative and relatively down to earth. People are encouraged to contribute beyond their immediate area, and the leadership team values straightforward advice backed by good information.
  
Finance is seen as an important part of the business rather than simply a reporting function. The opportunity is to build on what is already in place, bring a sharper commercial lens and help shape how the organisation approaches future decisions.
  
The Role
  • Work alongside the leadership team on business priorities, future plans and key commercial decisions
  • Bring greater visibility to the factors driving revenue, margin, costs and overall performance
  • Lead annual planning and regular forecasting, giving the business a realistic view of what lies ahead
  • Build models and business cases around investment, pricing, growth opportunities and operational change
  • Turn financial and operational information into clear recommendations that leaders can act on
  • Ask the right questions, test assumptions and provide constructive challenge when decisions are being made
  • Maintain close oversight of cashflow, working capital and the organisation’s wider financial position
  • Oversee management and statutory reporting, controls, compliance and relationships with external advisors
  • Improve the quality, speed and usefulness of reporting across the business
  • Lead a compact and dynamic team and create the capacity for finance to contribute more widely
  
Your Profile
  • A strong background in broad senior finance roles, with experience contributing beyond the traditional reporting and control remit
  • A recognised accounting qualification, supported by sound experience across financial management and commercial decision support
  • The judgement and confidence to contribute meaningfully alongside senior leaders
  • Strong forecasting, modelling and analytical skills, with the ability to identify the commercial story behind the numbers
  • Experience contributing to pricing, investment decisions, business cases, profitability or performance improvement
  • A practical communication style and the confidence to question assumptions without making things unnecessarily complicated
  • The ability to think beyond finance while still maintaining reliable reporting, controls and delivery
  • A hands-on and adaptable approach, with the willingness to move between wider business priorities and detailed financial issues
  • Full, unrestricted working rights for New Zealand and be based in or actively relocating to Christchurch

job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
The Opportunity
As the Finance Manager you’ll be joining an established organisation in a permanent role that sits at the centre of its financial operations. Reporting to a senior executive, this is a hands-on leadership opportunity with broad responsibility across management reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cashflow, compliance and process improvement.
  
This role offers the chance to partner closely with senior stakeholders, providing clear financial insight that supports operational and commercial decision-making across the business. You’ll lead day-to-day finance activity while overseeing a small established team, helping ensure strong controls, accurate reporting and continuous improvement.
  
The Company
This organisation is well established, values-led and known for its collaborative and relationship-focused culture. It operates in a professional environment where service quality, sound judgement and strong internal support functions are all highly valued.
  
With a stable platform and a well-regarded team, the business offers the opportunity to step into a visible and trusted finance leadership role with genuine breadth and influence.
  
The Role
  • Key member of the wider business services function, partnering closely with senior leadership across the organisation
  • Preparation of periodic management reporting including profit and loss, balance sheet, cashflow, KPI dashboards and commentary, together with ownership of month-end processes and reconciliations
  • Management of budgeting, forecasting, profitability analysis and scenario modelling to support annual planning and wider commercial decision-making
  • Oversight of tax compliance, financial controls, system integrity, receivables and payables, and support for payroll review and related compliance processes
  • Leadership of specialist compliance-related administration through direct reports, ensuring strong oversight, reporting integrity and ongoing process improvement
  • Management of banking relationships, user access and authority controls, plus preparation of year-end workpapers and liaison with external advisors on annual reporting matters
  • People leadership of a small finance and administration team
  
Your Profile
  • Chartered Accountant or equivalent preferred, or comparable senior finance experience in a hands-on leadership role
  • At least five years’ finance experience, ideally within a professional services or service-based environment
  • Strong management accounting, budgeting, forecasting and financial analysis capability, including confidence with modelling and commercial insight
  • Advanced Excel skills and strong systems capability across Microsoft Office and modern finance platforms, with dashboard reporting exposure advantageous
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate financial information for non-financial stakeholders and build credible internal relationships
  • High level of accuracy, confidentiality and discretion, paired with a hands-on, proactive and commercially minded approach
  • Hold full, unrestricted working rights for New Zealand and be based in or actively relocating to Christchurch

job.title: General Manager
job.description:
The Opportunity
Very rarely does the chance come up to take the lead role in a long established wholesaler of tyres based in the fastest growing city in NZ. This is a true General Manager role, with accountability for the operational delivery of agreed strategy and direct leadership of the SLT.
  
With responsibility for business performance, operational efficiency and risk management, you will steer a market leader with deep distribution capability through the challenging curves of a competitive industry, delivering market share growth through setting clear leadership expectations that ensure consistent value led leadership across the organisation.
  
You will have a number of executive objectives across strategy including divisional plans, financial budgets, business priorities and key performance indicators – and the ability to pivot to maintain alignment as the market changes.

The Company
Value Tyres Limited (VTL) is an established wholesaler of tyres based across 10 locations nationally who boast over 50 years successful trading. With a growing team, VTL maintains the family ownership and family feel through a strong commitment to culture maintained by valuing customers both internal and external, taking ownership to find solutions, and leading with innovation and integrity.

The Role
  • Leadership of the senior leadership team comprising four heads of department
  • Design and sustaining of a cohesive operating model across divisions
  • Owning succession planning within the leadership structure
  • Relationship development and management with senior external stakeholders in both supplier and customer areas
  • Drive performance visibility and accountability through KPIs, dashboards and regular reviews
  • Lead the annual business planning and budgeting process with the SLT and monitor performance against budget
  • Ensure compliance with regulatory, administrative and operational requirements, that key business risks are identified and evaluated, and that VTL carries adequate insurance coverage
  • Provide visible leadership for a safe and healthy workplace, ensuring compliance with policies and good practice

Your Profile
  • Proven experience leading a multi-site or multi-function operation through an engaged Senior Leadership Team
  • Track record of creating alignment across functions and holding leaders accountable to delivery
  • Commercially astute. Comfortable balancing service, margin, cost control, working capital and growth outcomes
  • Experienced leading annual planning and budgeting cycles and managing performance against plan with corrective actions
  • Comfortable becoming “knowledgeable enough” across multiple operational areas to add value without micromanaging functional leads
  • Pragmatic, decisive problem-solver who makes timely calls using practical judgement and clear rationale
  • Personally organised and resilient. Maintains prioritisation and operating cadence during change, ambiguity and peak workload
  • Hold full, unrestricted working rights for New Zealand and be based in or actively relocating to Christchurch

job.title: Multiple Accounts Receivable Opportunities
job.description:
The Opportunity 
You’ve been managing debtor ledgers, chasing payments, reconciling statements and sorting customer queries for long enough to know what good AR work feels like. 
I’ve got two Accounts Receivable opportunities right now. Different businesses, different setups, but both need someone who actually enjoys the work and wants to do it well.

The Role
You’ll own the day-to-day AR process: raising invoices, applying payments, following up on overdue accounts, reconciling statements, and dealing with the queries that land on your desk. You’ll also get the chance to tidy up processes that are a bit messy and help the wider finance team keep cash moving. One role has more senior flavour, mentoring others and improving how things run. The other is solid hands-on AR where accuracy and relationships matter.

You’ll use the usual tools (Xero or similar, Excel, email) and talk to both internal people and external customers. Some days will be steady. Others will be busy when month-end hits or a big account needs sorting.

Your Profile
These roles reward people who like clear ownership, steady variety, and seeing the direct result of their work on the business’s cash position. You’ll work with finance teams that value getting it right over ticking boxes, and there’s room to suggest better ways of doing things.

If that sounds like the kind of AR role you’ve been looking for, get in touch. Tell me a bit about your recent experience and which of the two feels closer to what you want next.
